business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Commodity Trade in Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49-54: Freedom of Establishment for the SAS as a French national entity
Union Customs Code, Regulation (EU) No 952/2013: cross-border commodity trade clearance and customs transit framework
Convention between France and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 26 November 2013, in force)
France-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 26 November 2007, in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59-4 and R.561-1 to R.561-23 (AML/CFT and beneficial-owner obligations); Article L.561-2-2 and Article L.561-47 CMF (UBO registration and restricted access); Décret n° 2021-1610 of 9 December 2021 (digitalized UBO register, restricted consultation); Arrêté of 2 September 2020 (UBO declaration content and transmission format); Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843, transposed into French law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutes of the SAS (Articles of Association)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders represented by a French avocat; notary only in cases of real-property contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized deed solely where contributions include real property; otherwise signed private deed with avocat certification; domestic execution requires no apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the foreign shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961; for non-Hague Convention states, consular legalization by the French Embassy; EU Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 exemption applies within the EU

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of foreign UBO and of the SAS President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport or identity authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy with Hague Apostille for non-EU issuers; simple certified copy for EU/EEA issuers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate authorization / board resolution of foreign corporate shareholder approving SAS incorporation and appointment of management
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-EU issuers; EU Regulation (EU) 2016/1191 exemption for EU-member issuers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, managers, officers and UBOs against the OFAC SDN list (given USD Swift LC payment rails), UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, French GEMON asset-freeze list under Article L.562-1 et seq. CMF, and identification of politically exposed persons (PEPs) under Article L.561-10 CMF. Screening must be documented with timestamped reports and re-run within five business days before the incorporation filing; any positive match triggers enhanced due diligence, reporting to TRACFIN under Article L.561-15 CMF, and refusal of the transaction unless a valid EU/UN/OAC freeze exemption applies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (procedures.inpi.fr); name availability is verified against the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via Infogreffe and the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French-language compliance under Law n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Loi Toubon); the corporate name must be written in Latin script using full French accented characters; a foreign-language or non-Latin denomination is admissible only where a French-language equivalent is recorded in the articles of association; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing RNE/RCS name and must not misstate the legal form (SAS).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal via the Guichet Unique portal. The applicant may: (1) remove the conflicting tokens and resubmit immediately on the same portal; (2) request re-examination by the Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of refusal; (3) file an administrative appeal with the INPI coordination unit where the refusal is attributed to registry error; and (4) petition the President of the Tribunal de Commerce by assignation within one month of notification seeking annulment of the refusal under Articles L.123-4 and R.123-2 of the Code de commerce. A parallel civil action for cancellation of a confusingly similar existing name may be brought before the Tribunal Judiciaire.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional. A pure virtual mailbox is not accepted for ISIC 4633 dairy commodity trading. Use of an INPI-approved domiciliation company under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce is permitted, provided the SAS maintains a physical office presence in France, is reachable during business hours by DGCCRF and the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects, and retains original customs and sanitary documentation at the registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability within the first 18 months, based on DGCCRF probability-based national control plans for wholesale foodstuff operators, customs post-clearance documentary audits under the Union Customs Code, and TRACFIN typologies relating to trade-based money laundering in dairy commodity flows.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS Articles of Association and UBO/piercing legal file by a French avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French law firm (avocat) engaged by the founding shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee; mandatory notarization is not required where capital is contributed exclusively in cash

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a legal announcements gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-line tariff set by ministerial order for the relevant judicial department

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration duty (droit de greffe) and allocation of SIREN/SIRET identifiers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, collected via the INPI Guichet Unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by decree of the garde des sceaux for company registrations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI Guichet Unique electronic filing handling fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name availability verification and certificate of non-confusion (dénomination sociale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce / Infogreffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry search tariff or prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation agreement for 12 months, including physical premises and postal handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI-approved société de domiciliation under Article L.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 50-60 per month

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostilles and consular legalization of foreign shareholder and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cour d'appel or competent foreign apostille authority / French consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff of approximately EUR 25-40 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and GEMON sanctions screening and UBO risk file set-up
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance/KYC service provider retained by the shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a TRACFIN-grade due diligence and sanctions-screening file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of corporate transaction bank account and capital deposit compliance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for professional corporate account opening fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée) and R.223-1 et seq.; Civil Code provisions on contributions are supplementary.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry), France, operating through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr / Infogreffe.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formulaire M0 (Cerfa n° 15679*04) together with constitutional SAS bylaws (statuts), declaration of beneficial ownership, and Kbis application.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for SAS and no mandatory escrow account; the bylaws must state the capital, and any unpaid portion must be scheduled therein. If in-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report, capital payment certification is made by the auditor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company accepts subscriptions to its issued share capital as recorded in the registry of shareholders; that the temporary management and each subscriber irrevocably approve the amount and allocation of shares; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office established in the bylaws is adopted as the official legal seat, and the French Commercial Registry (Greffe) is instructed to file the incorporation dossier; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name], as President, and [Name], as General Manager, are appointed with full powers to represent the company and to complete all statutory registrations, bank account opening, and licensing applications; and that all prior actions taken by the founders and temporary managers are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Search and Founder Identity Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI national trademark database and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce records via Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on data.inpi.fr for identical trademarks and a corporate name check on Infogreffe; verify that the proposed SAS name is available and does not infringe prior rights; preserve the independently generated search evidence for submission with the M0 dossier.
required_dossiers: Valid identity documents of all subscribers
Residential or business address proof of proposed President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is refused for identical or confusing similarity, adopt a new distinctive name and re-run the search before proceeding to the bylaws drafting step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of SAS Constitutional Bylaws and Governance Structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders' legal counsel and, if real property is contributed, a French notaire; otherwise no notarial deed is mandatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French 'statuts constitutifs' in accordance with Code de commerce Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20; set the corporate purpose to wholesale trade in whole and skimmed milk powder (ISIC 46.33Z alignment), registered office, share capital, President powers, optional General Manager, and share transfer restrictions; require each founder to sign every page and initial each annex, and execute President acceptance letter.
required_dossiers: Subscription schedule listing shareholders and share counts
Certificate by founder confirming no criminal incompatibility for management
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the registry identifies missing statutory clauses, execute a corrective riders agreement or new signed version and restart the submission with the rectified bylaws.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Capital and Issuance of Capital Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution (bank) or notary escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deposit the declared share capital in a blocked bank account in France or into a notary client account; obtain a written certificate confirming full subscription and payment and stating the account holder is the company in formation; for in-kind contributions, file at the next step the auditor's contribution report if the value is material under R.223-4.
required_dossiers: Bank capital blocking certificate or notarial escrow certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is refused due to missing proof of payment, obtain corrected bank ledger records and submit a new certificate; no M0 filing is made until the certificate is clean.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Dossier through the Single Formalities Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique operated by Infogreffe on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; submitted to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Formulaire M0 (Cerfa no. 15679*04) online; attach signed bylaws, capital certificate, beneficial owner declaration (using the standard INSEE/Greffe template), President identity documents, and proof of payment of registry fees; submit electronically and retrieve the dated acknowledgement with a provisional application number.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of Greffe fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the portal issues a query or rejection notice, correct the flagged fields in an amended declaration, upload omitted documents, and resubmit within the given opposition period; retain original acknowledgement for cost recovery.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration at the Trade Register and Issuance of Kbis, SIREN and SIRET
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation by the registry officer, await formal enrollment with the Registre National des Entreprises; obtain the Kbis certificate evidencing legal existence; INSEE automatically allocates SIREN and SIRET identifiers and the APE/NAF code, expected 46.33Z; verify data on the Kbis includes correct address and appointees.
required_dossiers: Submitted M0 and supporting PDF signed
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Kbis contains typographical errors, file a request for rectification ('rectification d'une erreur matérielle') with the registry, attaching the original decision of the legal representatives; if not printed within SLA, expedite via registry complaint desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance Ratification and Legal Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (JAL) for a French company; ministry registrar for beneficial-owner update
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after Kbis, publish the required incorporation notice in an authorized legal journal; hold a founder/shareholder or board resolution ratifying pre-formation acts and appointing officers as reflected in the Kbis; prepare the minutes in the corporate register; file the beneficial owner update and any change of governance with Infogreffe if it differs from the M0.
required_dossiers: Notice of incorporation to legal gazette (copy)
Ratifying resolutions and officer acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late publication is cured by immediate publication with explanatory statement and payment of any applicable late-filing penalty; governance omissions are cured by a written resolutive resolution filed as an 'acte déposé'.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations (DDPP) / Préfecture and Direction Générale de l'Alimentation for food-sector sanitary registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Déclaration d'activité du secteur alimentaire (DGCCRF/DDPP sanitary registration for storage and wholesale distribution of dairy products), supplemented where applicable by ICPE registration for cold-storage equipment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) France
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Warehousing operations below 1,500 m² are normally exempt from systematic EIA; ICPE déclaration registration applies for refrigerated warehouses using non-halogenated systems above 150 kW; full EIA only if ammonia refrigeration or hazardous waste storage triggers substantive codes 1150, 1150B and 2663 respectively.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharges to public sewer must respect local wastewater pre-treatment limits (e.g., pH 5.5-9.5, total suspended solids <600 mg/L); refrigeration refrigerant leakage limited to maximum 2% per installation per year under F-gas Regulation; milk powder waste and cleaning sludge must be handled as non-hazardous waste with transfer consignment note.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire safety certificate from Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for warehouse facilities exceeding 100-person occupancy or with refrigeration machinery; obtain structural load inspection certificate for storage racks; obtain occupational health clearance from CARSAT/OPP for workplace access, cold-environment exposure, and manual handling.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) and Direction Régionale des Douanes et Droits Indirects for customs/VAT on import-export; official portal: impots.gouv.fr and pro.douane.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SAS in France must (1) file Articles of Association with the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (now through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) to obtain an INSEE identification (SIREN/SIRET); (2) apply for a French VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire) via the Service des Impôts des Entreprises for the registered office using Form 326-PFG for regular filing or Form 3526 for EU sales; (3) submit a non-EU entity's ultimate parent, director/manager identification and a copy of a bank account certificate; (4) await delivery of the FR SIREN two-digit key and a provisional French VAT registration certificate; (5) for import/export activity, obtain an EORI number (FR followed by SIREN) through pro.douane.gouv.fr. Liquidation of minor errors requires a rectification filing with DGFiP; mandatory designation of a tax representative for non-EU principals applying for VAT refunds or direct customs clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box pass-through election exists under French domestic law; an SAS is per se subject to corporate income tax (IS). Available elections include: (1) option for normal corporate income tax if a fiscal integration regime applies under Article 223 A CGI, allowing a tax group with a 95%+ parent; (2) election under Article 239 bis A CGI to be treated as a tax-transparent partnership under strict statutory and joint-ownership conditions (limited to unlisted SCS/SCA, not SAS); (3) option for VAT franchise not available to an SAS because it exceeds the small-enterprise thresholds by statute; (4) hybrid mismatch design is constrained by DAC6 reporting and Article 212 bis CGI — no unilateral check-the-box, but upstream foreign entities may file form 8832 in their own jurisdiction to alter French branch/conduit result.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum registration threshold for an SAS performing taxable wholesale supplies in France; a compulsory registration is due from the first taxable transaction. The domestic franchise exemption may apply only to entity types demonstrating a tax-exclusive turnover below EUR 85,000 for supply of goods (gemeine rule) or EUR 37,500 for services, and does not apply to an SAS conducting merchant wholesale of dairy powders where the economic activity is taxable by default; a foreign company with no fixed establishment is entitled to distance-sales registration only above EUR 35,000 B2C threshold for another EU seller, but a French-domiciled SAS has no beneficial threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing for all French B2B transactions under Law 2022-1157 (Facturation électronique) enforced from 2024 for large taxpayers and from 2026 for all taxable persons, transmitted through certified dematerialization platforms (PDP) or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). Each invoice must satisfy prescribed structured data fields (factur-X/UBL) and be reported in near-real-time to DGFiP using a certified API (no digital stamping applies); customs export declarations are cleared via the DELTA/GCC system integrated with the Single Window, and a failed or altered fiscal data transmission leads to rejection of the invoice and a 15 EUR per-invoice penalty (Article 1737 CGI).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies under Article 262-I-1° CGI to tangible goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by or on behalf of the seller, evidenced by customs declaration; zero-rating extends to transport services directly linked to the export (Article 262-I-2°) and to intra-Community supply of goods if the purchaser possesses a valid EU VAT ID and the goods leave the seller's territory (Article 262-I-3°). For cross-border services supplied to a non-taxable EU customer or offshore principal, the place of supply determines whether VAT is due; an exporter must substantiate the actual removal of goods with transport contracts, loading risk and delivery terms (CIF/FOB), and for dairy commodity trading, the zero-rating cannot be claimed for goods retained in an EU customs warehouse or consumed in France.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation via DELTA-X, EMCS/GCC) proving customs release for exit from the EU customs territory
Bill of Lading (Connaissement) or CMR / AWB citing the French exporter of record, chapter 1–ISIC 4633 goods description, gross weight and destination outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (Attestation de Change / Banque de France certificate) evidencing that export payment was received in an authorized French bank account in convertible currency
Commercial invoice bearing the buyer's identity, incoterms and exact milk-powder specification (HS 0401/0402)
Transport document (for non-EU cargo: airway bill or seaway bill; for EU route to non-EU: transit transport document T1 or electronic exit summary ECS-D)
Register of export proofs and copy of the buyer's written confirmation of receipt at the declared non-EU port of destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or substantively defective export zero-rating triggers immediate VAT reversal with statutory interest and penalties: (1) 5% per quarter of the principal amount under Article 1731 CGI; (2) 80% fraudulent-claims penalty under Article 1737 CGI where the exporter issued false customs declarations or forged bills of lading; (3) administrative confiscation of exported goods (Article 414-3 Customs Code); (4) personal liability under Article 1753-bis CGI against the managing shareholder/director for concealment of grossly inflated export invoices; (5) an importer/exporter CSCE deregistration and six-month customs bank guarantee upon repeated violations. The recovery window is extended to six years in tax fraud cases, and a criminal customs offence entailing up to 30,000 EUR fine per declaration is counted, with clawback of the VAT refund plus 40% late-payment surcharge.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting in conjunction with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy and Finance) for foreign exchange control policy and balance-of-payments reporting; EU-level competence under the Single Euro Payments Area and the free movement of capital principle (TFEU Art. 63).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully and freely convertible within France and the euro area. No prior foreign-exchange approval is required for current-account transactions (trade in goods and services, income distributions and profit remittances) or for inward direct investment. Capital-account operations are liberalized subject to prudential monitoring; the only binding requirements are statistical reporting obligations to the Banque de France for cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 per calendar month (balance-of-payments reporting), and EU/UN sanctions screening of all counterparties. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted once corporate formalities (board approval, distributable reserves, withholding tax analysis under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive) are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export proceeds surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion requirements. Exporters may hold foreign currency proceeds freely in euro or foreign-currency accounts with authorized intermediaries. However, the Banque de France requires: (a) declaration of all cross-border settlements exceeding EUR 50,000 on a monthly aggregated basis via the authorized intermediary bank; (b) substantiation of export receipts by commercial invoices, transport documents, and the related EUR1/ATR or customs export declarations; (c) compliance with EU sanctions and anti-money-laundering screening on the paying bank and the underlying trade file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte courant) for trade settlement, collection and disbursement; segregated Capital Escrow Account or blocked sub-account for share-capital injection prior to Court Clerk registration
Operational Account in EUR and USD with dedicated SWIFT correspondence lines; Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) available for the constitution-stage capital deposit

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (Corporate and Investment Banking)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account specialized in commodity trade finance, supply-chain finance and documentary credit issuance/confirmation
Operational account and trade-finance facility; structured commodity finance desks for dairy-import programmes
Operational account for mid-cap corporate French SAS entities; corporate e-banking and capital escrow capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for collection-side receipts and disbursements, but LOW for end-to-end treasury autonomy. Legal constraints: an offshore (non-EEA) digital EMI may not provide payment services in France unless it holds an EU/EEA licence passported under PSD2 into the French market via the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) filing, or establishes a French branch. A UK-based EMI post-Brexit lacks passporting rights and would require full ACPR licensing or reliance on a French partner bank. EEA-licensed EMIs may operate through the single-passport regime but are subject to: (i) safeguarding of client funds in segregated accounts; (ii) SCA/PSD2 authentication; (iii) prohibition on granting credit; (iv) ACPR registration as a payment services agent/principal where local distribution occurs. For commodity trade treasury involving commercial LC operations, an EMI cannot substitute for a licensed credit institution; EMIs are therefore acceptable only as auxiliary rails for small-balance collections, not for documentary credit or escrow functions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical KYC interview of the SAS legal representative (Président) is generally required by all tier-1 French banks at the initial onboarding stage, particularly where the shareholder chain is non-resident; in-person attendance at the branch (or a visiting notary/bank officer remote-video session accepted under strictly defined ACPR-aligned video-identification procedures) is permissible in practice, but most banks' internal policies insist on a physical meeting or a live video-verification session combined with apostilled corporate documentation. Remote opening (via e-signature and videoconference) is technically available for account holders with a French tax presence or established French group parent; however, for a foreign-owned FR_SAS undertaking cross-border commodity trading, enhanced due diligence typically adds: notarized and apostilled statutes, an original banking-residency certificate from the ultimate beneficial owner, three years of audited financial statements of the parent, and a formal in-person or videoconference interview of the legal representative. The practical mandate is therefore: at least one physical presence of the statutory representative and provision of wet-ink signatures on the account mandate for dual-authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The account-opening bank flags the ultimate beneficial ownership chain as opaque because the SAS is a newly incorporated French vehicle wholly owned by a non-resident foreign holding with no French operating history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate organizational chart down to the natural-person UBOs; apostilled and notarized extract of the K-bis, Articles of Association/Statutes of the SAS, and the parent's certificate of incorporation; LEI codes of all intermediate entities; a notarized UBO declaration (Déclaration de Bénéficiaire Effectif) filed with the French Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; letter of explanation of the group's commercial substance; references from a recognized international bank for the parent; and audited financial statements of the parent for the last three fiscal years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection is small relative to projected turnover, or immediate large-value trade flows are anticipated, triggering a funds-source/wealth-screening alert and an expectation of disproportionate transaction volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow projection, execution contracts (purchase agreements and framework supply agreements with named counterparties), board resolution fixing the initial capital and treasury policy; proof of funds (parent's bank statements, audited accounts showing distributable reserves); a written declaration of the economic rationale (import/distribution of milk powder from approved origins); commercial invoices and pre-contracts showing the exact goods, quantities, and delivery schedules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or destination jurisdictions include sanctions-sensitive or high-AML-risk provenance for dairy commodities (e.g., transshipment through freight hubs), prompting enhanced screening alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening reports (EU, UN, OFAC) performed on all counterparties, carrying banks and end-buyers; certificate of origin and health certificates (EU third-country milk-powder import requiring EU health attestation and approved-establishment list); transport documentation (CMR note, bill of lading, customs declaration via DELTA/SW import); end-beneficiary/customer declarations; full audit trail of purchase orders, invoices, and insurance certificates; and the bank's internal negative-media check with the company's documented rebuttal where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The bank perceives the SAS's trade cycle as unverifiable because trade documents (invoice, bill of lading, customs entry) are not managed on an open-account basis, and clients request clean TT wires on a fully advanced-payment basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master trade finance dossier containing: duly signed commercial contracts (INCOTERMS and payment terms), pro-forma/commercial invoice sequences, provenance certificates, carrier booking confirmations, customs transit declarations, and the French customs clearance file; a board-approved treasury and trade-finance policy detailing the payment sequencing (documentary collections or LC where military-grade documentation is not available); an undertaking to route first transactions through Commercial LC or Documentary Collection, converting to open account only after bank-established performance history.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the shareholder remits the subscribed capital either (i) to a notary-sealed Capital Escrow Account of the SAS opened in France before incorporation, or (ii) directly to the SAS's operational account after K-bis registration, in each case by SWIFT MT103/TT. The wire must use ISO 20022 purpose-code 'EQUI' (or 'INCA' for capital increase) and include the SAS's name, LEI and the reference of the capital subscription resolution. Bank verification requires the notary certificate of deposit (attestation du dépositaire des fonds), the deed of incorporation, a statement of no registration within eight days, and the UBO declaration. Funds must be free of any third-party encumbrance; for loans a shareholder loan agreement and interest-rate conditions aligned with French thin-capitalization transfer pricing rules are required. For non-EU remitters, requisite supporting record: source-of-funds evidence (audited accounts, dividend resolution of the remitting entity, or disposal contract).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails for a French SAS paying foreign milk-powder suppliers and logistics parties: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 single-payment TT wires in EUR/USD on a maturity-matched basis; (b) Documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600 (sight or usance) issued by the French bank in favour of suppliers, with negotiation under the supplier's corresponding bank; (c) Standby LCs for advance-payment performance security; (d) Documentary Collections under URC 522 (Documents against Payment / Documents against Acceptance) as the intermediate control option; (e) domestic SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro-denominated payments within the EEA; and (f) supply-chain finance programmes (approved payables financing) for recurring imports. Settlement-risk control includes matching of MT103 field 70/Remittance Information with the underlying commercial invoice, use of dense SWIFT category codes (e.g., TRAD for trade), and daily zero-balancing into a concentration account at BNP Paribas/Société Générale.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX forwards (maturity ≤ 12 months) executed with a licensed French credit institution under an ISDA/FXA master confirmation
EUR/CNY, EUR/CHF and EUR/USD foreign-exchange swaps (FXSW) to cover the conversion timing mismatch between trade payables and receivables
Currency options (vanilla call/put, exchange-traded and OTC) for asymmetric protection of commodity-trade margins

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for financially restricted emerging-market currencies where onshore deliverability is legally unavailable to a French resident, subject to internal policy and EMIR collateral rules
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS) on term loans if the treasury extends financing into receivables-bearing foreign-currency invoices
Short-tenored FX swap lines under the Group Treasury addendum, governed by ISDA 2011 EMIR portfolio reconciliation, margining and ACPR/ESMA clearing-obligation checks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt annuel des comptes annuels, du rapport de gestion et du rapport du commissaire aux comptes (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Guichet unique des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year F/Y no later than June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing injunction carrying a daily delay penalty up to EUR 2,500 per day after formal notice; further delay exposes company to administrative strike-off (radiation) and thereby loss of limited liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration annuelle de résultats d'impôt sur les sociétés (formulaire n°2065 and required annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year fiscal year: by May 3 of the following year (extended to May 4/5 for e-filing); for other fiscal years, within 3 months of the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment penalty plus 0.20% monthly interest (interest at 0.40% after 6 months); fixed fine from EUR 750 to EUR 2,500 for failure to file; persistent delinquency can trigger enforced tax assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaration of Beneficial Owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) – annual reconfirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each year within 15 days following the anniversary of the company's registration in the RCS; also re-file within 30 days of any shareholding transfer resulting in change of beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 5,000 per individual and EUR 15,000 per legal entity for failure to declare; registration or publication acts become ineffective, leading to prohibitions on dividends and share transfers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of accounts (decision collective des associés) preceding the statutory filing of audited accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record (minutes registered and filed with Guichet unique as part of accounts deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; subsequent filing must occur within one month of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold approval by statutory deadline makes the balance-sheet filing null and risks nullity claims; judges may rule dissolution of the SAS in case of urgent irregularity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (commissaire aux comptes) for SAS if, at fiscal year-end, the entity exceeds any two of the following thresholds: total balance sheet > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average permanent staff > 50 employees. An audit is also mandatory regardless of thresholds for subsidiaries exceeding certain consolidation criteria or as triggered by shareholders' request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (Règlement ANC n°2016-07, incorporating PCG); IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements of listed entities. Full disclosure of annex and faithful true and fair view is required under Code de commerce articles L.123-12 et seq.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must re-confirm its beneficial owners annually within 15 days after the RCS anniversary date. Every shareholding transfer must be reported to the beneficial-owner register and filed through the Guichet unique within 30 days of execution; the annual filing likewise identifies any modifications. Failure to maintain an exact current UBO register suspends corporate acts and dividend distributions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des associés et actions)
Register of Directors (Registre des mouvements de titres and board/management minutes)
Beneficial Owner Register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – 2,500 per annum depending on provision of French registered office, mail handling, and legal representation services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 15,000 per annum for an SME-range SAS with dairy commodity trading turnover in the EUR 8-20 million band; higher amounts apply where consolidated or group audits are required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate; reduced 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small companies with annual turnover below EUR 10 million.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays. Principal incentives: Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR) at 30% on eligible R&D expenses up to EUR 100 million (5% above); Crédit d'Impôt Innovation (CII) at 20% for SME innovation expenses; reduced 15% CIT on first EUR 42,500; French IP-patent box (10% effective rate on qualifying net royalty income); participation exemption on 95% of dividends received from qualifying subsidiaries; no withholding on qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary dividends.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed-year expiry under French law: losses carried forward indefinitely, but annual utilisation capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; optional one-year carryback capped at EUR 1,000,000 and refunded over five years.
